title: Neonatal Cardiac Scaffolds: Novel Matrices for Regenerative Studies
protocol: Euthanize a neonatal mouse by decapitation with a single-use blade.
Swab the thorax with 70% ethanol.
Dissect the skin from the chest by cutting it away from the chest wall with standard scissors while pulling the skin laterally with a pair of #5 forceps.
Perforate the abdomen just inferior to the sternum with scissors, cutting through the abdominal wall.
Grasp the xiphoid process with #5 forceps and retract the sternum rostrally from the body.
Cut through the ribs on either side of the chest with scissors.
Reflect the rib cage superiorly with forceps to reveal the heart.
Bluntly dissect the two main lobes of the thymus by pulling laterally with #5 forceps, exposing the arch of the aorta and the caval and pulmonary veins.
Transect the major arteries from the aortic arch and the aorta itself with 10 cm spring scissors.
Retain the aorta between the base of the heart and the brachiocephalic artery.
Grasp the ends of the severed vessels with #5 forceps to reflect the heart forward, separating it from the trachea and esophagus.
Transect the pulmonary vasculature and other major veins by cutting between the lungs and the heart on both sides of the heart with spring scissors.
Remove the heart from the mediastinum using forceps by grasping the severed ends of the major vessels.
Place the heart in a 60 mm culture dish containing sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Draw a 4 cm section of PE 50 tubing in an alcohol flame to create a smaller, thinner catheter.
Trim the ends of the drawn tubing with a blade to meet the dimensions specified.
Melt a flange onto the opening at the thin end of the tubing by pointing it into the flame briefly.
Fill a 12 ml syringe with PBS and assemble the catheter by placing a 3-way stopcock on the syringe.
Add a 22 G x 1 needle to the stopcock and drive the needle through the septum.
Slide the drawn PE tubing catheter onto the needle.
Irrigate the assembled parts with PBS, ensuring all air bubbles have been removed.
Insert the catheter into the aorta of the isolated heart without extending past the aortic valve.
Ligate the catheter with one tie of 7-0 suture and rest the flange proximally against the tie to create a tight seal.
Observe the catheterization under magnification while gently perfusing the heart with PBS.
Ensure there are no leaks in the system and that the tissue blanches homogeneously as latent blood is removed.
Place the septum into the neck of the inlet adaptor and seal it by folding the sides over the glass.
Attach a reservoir filled with 60 ml of 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in distilled water to generate 20 mm Hg pressure.
Perfuse the heart with 1% SDS for 14 hours until the heart becomes translucent and no tissue remains observable.
Flush the system up to the stopcock with the remaining SDS solution and replace it with 10 ml of distilled water.
Perfuse the heart with 10 ml of 1% Triton X-100 diluted in distilled water, followed by another 10 ml of distilled water.
Finally, perfuse the heart with 60 ml of PBS containing 1x penicillin streptomycin (Pen-Strep).
Store the heart in PBS with 1x Pen-Strep at 4°C.
Maintain the catheter in the aorta if perfusion is required post-decellularization.
Cut and remove the catheter after loosening the suture tie if perfusion is not needed.
Prepare a digest of decellularized ECM or control heart using 200 μg/ml proteinase K, 50 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl2, 0.45% Tween 20 in 10 mM Tris (pH 8.3).
Incubate the tissue at 55°C with agitation until completely dissolved.
Quantitate the DNA content of the homogenate using a DNA binding assay.
Fix decellularized, recellularized, or control P3 hearts in 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash the tissue in PBS three times.
Place the tissue in a solution of 7.5% sucrose in 0.1 M phosphate buffer until it sinks.
Change to a 15% sucrose in 0.1 M phosphate buffer solution and wait until it sinks.
Warm the tissue to 37°C, replace half of its volume with gelatin solution in 15% sucrose & 0.1 M phosphate buffer, and equilibrate overnight.
Increase gelatin concentrations stepwise through 1%, 2.5%, 5%, and finally twice at 7.5%.
Place the samples in cryomolds using fresh 7.5% gelatin.
Restore the shape of decellularized samples by perfusing liquid gelatin into chambers as hearts are molded.
Float the cryomolds on liquid nitrogen to freeze.
Store frozen samples at -80°C.
Cut sections with a cryostat to obtain 10 µm thick slices.
Bring the slide close to the section surface and observe the section move off onto the surface.
Dry the slides overnight and store at -80°C for future analysis.
Remove the slides from the freezer, equilibrate to room temperature.
Place the slides in a Coplin jar containing PBS for 20 min at 37°C to dissolve gelatin.
Stain cut sections with Hematoxylin and Eosin.
Place the slides in a Coplin jar.

Expose hydrated slides to Hematoxylin for 45 sec, tap water for 1.5 min, buffer for 3 min, tap water for 1 min, bluing agent for 1.5 min, 80% ethanol for 1 min, Alcoholic Eosin Y for 8 sec, 80% ethanol for 1 min, 100% ethanol for 1 min twice, clearing agent (xylene substitute) for 1 min three times.
Coverslip the slides with resin-based mounting medium.
Examine the slides microscopically to confirm the retention of ECM protein reactivity of the heart ECM.

Stain hydrated slides for collagen IV by treating them in a humidified chamber with 10% normal donkey serum (NDS) in phosphate buffered saline with 0.1% Triton-X100 (PBST) for 1 hr at room temperature (RT).
Replace the solution with the primary antibody of choice, diluted to an empirically determined dilution in 5% NDS / PBST.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash the slides with PBST three times.
Apply a secondary antibody conjugated with a fluorescent dye.
Incubate for 1 hr at room temperature.
Wash the slides with PBS three times.
Stain the slides with DAPI.
Examine the slides with a fluorescent microscope at 50 to 400X magnification.
Spray each pup with 70% ethanol and decapitate using a single-use blade.
Hold the pup between the thumb and forefinger while splitting the thorax at the midline with small sterile scissors to expose the thoracic cavity.
Apply pressure to allow the heart to protrude freely from the chest.
Cut the heart free of major vessels and atria, leaving only ventricular tissue.
Place each heart directly into a 50 ml tube containing ice-cold Calcium, Bicarbonate-free Hank's buffered saline solution with 20 mM 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid (CBFHH).
Aspirate the CBFHH and add fresh CBFHH (ice-cold) to the tube.
Wash the tissue by swirling it in the tube several times.
Decant the solution containing the hearts into a 60 mm plastic Petri dish.
Dissect latent atrial tissue from the hearts under magnification on ice.
Mince ventricles into homogenously sized small pieces.
Remove any separated non-ventricular tissue from the dish with forceps.
Transfer minced ventricular tissue into a sterile vial containing CBFHH solution and a sterile micro stir bar using pipette.
Allow tissue to sediment to the bottom of the vial, then remove CBFHH solution.
Prepare 50 ml enzyme solution consisting of 1.75 mg/ml trypsin and 20 µg/ml DNase II in CBFHH.
Add 5 ml enzyme solution to a tube containing minced ventricular tissue.
Place tube on magnetic stirrer and stir at constant rate (340 rpm) for 8 min.
Remove vial from stir plate and allow slurry to sediment for 3 min.
Pipette and discard initial digest supernatant.
Pipette a second 5 ml aliquot of the enzyme solution and add it to the digesting ventricle.
Stir for 8 min.
Allow it to sediment for another 3 min.
Prepare two 50 ml tubes, each containing 12 ml ice-cold fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Place a 40 µm cell strainer atop each tube.
Pipette the supernatant through the filter on tube 1.
Repeat the digestion process an additional 8 times, alternating the placement of the digest supernatant between the two tubes containing FBS.
Split the last supernatant equally between tubes 1 and 2 to ensure equal volumes in each tube.
Centrifuge the tubes containing the supernatant at 150 x g for 6 min at 4 °C.
Prepare five 100 mm tissue culture plates with 6 ml of media (Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Media (DMEM) with 10% FBS, 1x Pen-Strep, 1x L-glutamine) per plate.
Incubate these aliquots at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 30 min to equilibrate the media.
Aspirate the CBFHH enzyme mixture and resuspend the cells into the 30 ml of culture media prepared above, combining the cells from both collection tubes.
Return 6 ml of cell suspension to each of the 100 mm plates and incubate for 45 min at 37 °C.
Transfer non-adherent cells to 5 new dishes after incubation.
Re-incubate for 45 minutes.
Collect media and non-adherent cells from the dishes at the end of pre-plating.
Spin the collected media at 150 x g for 6 minutes.
Draw off excess media to achieve an approximate concentration of 4.0 x 10^5 cells per construct in 100 µl of perfusate.
Remove an aliquot for counting and viability testing.
Pretreat isolated heart matrix with culture media overnight before recellularization.
Assemble the elements of a Langendorff system.
Autoclave glass parts to assure sterility.
Ethylene oxide sterilize plastic parts to ensure sterility.
Mount various sub-units on the support stand in a laminar flow hood.
Fill the assembled system with 120 ml of tissue culture media.
Place catheterized heart matrix from previous steps into a 60 mm culture dish under magnification.
Connect a 1 ml syringe with 22 G x 1 needle loaded with cell suspension to the catheter.
Ensure assembly is free of air bubbles to avoid embolizing the heart.
Gently perfuse the 100 µl of cell suspension into the heart matrix via the coronary arteries.
Detach the syringe/needle combination once complete.
Secure a 22g blunt stub to the Luer fitting on the underside of the bioreactor heart jar lid.
Push the catheter onto the stub.
Start the peristaltic pump and observe that the flow proceeds as outlined.
Flow proceeds from the reservoir via the pump through the bubble trap to the catheter placed in the aorta.
Observe the flow of the cardiac circulation out of the veins and dripping from the apex, recirculating to the media reservoir.
